words.desc: A portable box-shaped instrument whose bellows are squeezed to push air past reeds.
A hollow-bodied stringed instrument with a round opening that needs no amplifier to be heard.
A very long wooden wind instrument with an upturned bell, played in Swiss mountain pastures.
A Scottish wind instrument where an air-filled bag under the arm feeds reeded drones.
A plucked stringed instrument with a round body covered by a tight skin like a drumhead.
A side-blown flute made from a single length of bamboo, played across India.
The largest and lowest-pitched drum, played with a soft beater or a foot pedal.
A four-stringed instrument with a long neck that plays the lowest notes in a band.
A large low-pitched woodwind instrument with a long folded tube and a double reed.
Hollow metal cups that ring with a clear tone when struck by a clapper.
A pair of small joined drums played with the hands, popular in Latin music.
A simple brass instrument without valves, used to sound military calls.
A pair of small shell-shaped clappers held in one hand and clicked together.
A large bowed string instrument played while seated and held upright between the knees.
A set of long hanging metal tubes that ring out when struck with a hammer.
A black wind instrument with a single reed and a straight cylindrical body.
Tall narrow single-headed drums from Cuba, played standing up with the palms.
A compact valved brass instrument with a conical bore and a mellow tone.
A hollow metal percussion piece struck with a stick to give a dry, clanking beat.
A thin round plate of brass or bronze that crashes loudly when struck.
A large double-headed barrel-shaped percussion instrument from South Asia, beaten with two sticks.
A long wooden wind instrument of Aboriginal Australia that produces a deep droning sound.
A goblet-shaped drum from West Africa, played with bare hands.
The largest and deepest bowed string instrument, played standing up or on a tall stool.
A set of percussion instruments that are struck to keep time in a band.
A solid-bodied stringed instrument whose sound is picked up magnetically and played through an amplifier.
A mid-sized conical brass instrument with valves, pitched like a tenor and sounding warm.
A violin as it is played in folk, country and dance music traditions.
A slender instrument held sideways and played by blowing across a mouth hole.
A brass instrument of coiled tubing with a wide bell, played with one hand inside it.
A percussion instrument of tuned steel bars struck with hard mallets, giving a bright ringing sound.
A large hanging metal disc that makes a deep resonant sound when hit with a mallet.
A stringed instrument with a long fretted neck that is strummed or plucked.
A small metal cup with a handle that rings when swung, often played in tuned choirs.
A small rectangular instrument played by blowing and drawing air through reed holes.
A small keyboard instrument with hand-worked bellows, common in Indian devotional singing.
A large triangular frame strung with many strings that are plucked by hand.
A keyboard instrument whose strings are plucked by quills when the keys are pressed.
A small metal frame held against the teeth whose flexible tongue is plucked to make a twang.
A small hollow toy pipe that buzzes when you hum into it.
An electronic instrument with a row of black and white keys and many built-in sounds.
A plucked stringed instrument with a rounded pear-shaped back, popular in Renaissance Europe.
An ancient handheld instrument with strings stretched from a crossbar to a hollow body.
A small pear-shaped instrument with pairs of metal strings, played with a pick.
A pair of hollow gourd rattles filled with seeds or beads, shaken in rhythm.
A large wooden-barred percussion instrument with resonator tubes underneath, giving a warm mellow tone.
A double-headed barrel-shaped percussion instrument used in South Indian classical music.
A slender woodwind instrument with a double reed and a piercing, nasal tone.
A small round clay wind instrument with finger holes, often shaped like an egg.
A keyboard instrument that produces sound by sending air through rows of pipes.
A set of hollow pipes of different lengths bound side by side and blown across the top.
A large keyboard instrument in which pressed keys make hammers strike tuned strings.
A tiny high-pitched woodwind held sideways, half the length of its larger orchestral cousin.
A simple end-blown pipe with finger holes, often the first instrument learned at school.
A trapezoid-shaped instrument from Kashmir with many strings struck by light wooden mallets.
A fretless Indian lute with a metal fingerboard and a skin-covered wooden body.
A bent brass-bodied woodwind instrument that is played with a single reed.
A double-reed wind instrument from North India, traditionally played at weddings and temples.
A long-necked Indian stringed instrument with a gourd body and many sympathetic strings.
A shallow drum with metal wires stretched under its bottom head, giving a sharp rattle.
A large brass instrument that wraps around the player's body, with a huge forward-facing bell.
A pair of ordinary eating utensils held back to back and clacked against the knee.
A tuned percussion instrument made from an oil barrel, hammered into dented note areas.
An electronic instrument that creates and shapes sounds using oscillators and filters.
A pair of small hand drums from India, played with the fingers and palms.
A small hand-held frame drum fitted with metal jingles that rattle when shaken.
A long-necked Indian string instrument that plays a continuous drone behind singers.
An electronic instrument played without touch, by moving the hands near two antennas.
Large copper bowls with skin heads, tuned to exact pitches by a foot pedal.
A steel rod bent into a three-sided shape and struck with a metal beater.
A large brass instrument whose pitch is changed by pushing and pulling a slide.
A brass instrument with three valves, played by buzzing the lips into a mouthpiece.
The largest and lowest-pitched brass instrument, with a wide bell that faces upward.
A small four-stringed instrument of Hawaiian fame, usually strummed with the fingers.
A large plucked South Indian instrument with a long fretted neck and gourd resonators.
A percussion instrument of metal bars with motor-driven fans in its resonators, giving a wavering tone.
A bowed four-stringed instrument held at the shoulder, with a mellow middle-range voice.
A small high-pitched stringed instrument that rests on the shoulder and is bowed.
A ridged metal laundry scrubbing frame played by scraping it with thimbles.
A percussion instrument made of wooden bars in a row, struck with small mallets.
